prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Final production source art for a 2D magical cyan water nest sprite animation. The two references establish STRICT palette, material, outline thickness, lighting and slightly top-down isometric camera. Generate a TRANSPARENT 2x2 square sprite atlas of FOUR isolated, consecutive water-entry impact drawings. These will be composited ON TOP of the existing flat pool: do NOT draw a nest, pond base, thick basin, standing water column or the incoming large droplet. Only the LOCAL water reaction at the water surface. Consistent subject center and ground-plane ellipse in every cell, plenty of transparent margins, no cell overlap. Reading left to right then top to bottom: 1) Tiny depressed oval water dimple with a dark teal central cavity and a very low thin raised circular lip; initial plop where a drop just penetrated the surface. 2) A SMALL LOW splash crown rising out of that same dimple, four to six short soft rounded water tips and only two tiny adjacent spray beads, open center; splash tips at most one-quarter the footprint width. This must look like a drop landing in water, NOT a raised bowl or ornate wavy nest. 3) The crown collapsing outward into a flatter broad low water collar with a rounded flowing edge, no tall crests and no spray beads; center almost level. 4) One thin clean horizontal elliptical ripple crest with a transparent center, subtle cyan/teal shadow along the outer edge and a narrow creamy pale aqua highlight, no large white glow. Its width about four times its height, smooth calm surface-wave shape, no solid filled oval. Same painted glossy turquoise water as references, warm aqua highlight upper-left, dark teal thin outer contour. Shape progression must be dimple -> short plop crown -> low outward wave -> thin traveling ripple. Effects should be delicate relative to the nest, physically readable at small game size. No text, labels, diagrams, grids, borders, white backdrop, cast shadows, extra objects, sparkles or magic circles. Actual transparent alpha. Use this atlas as real animation artwork, not a presentation mockup.
